comment: The harness's own dated deferrals, as reviewed data — the ONE machine-read home for every dated deferral sentence in the harness-OWNED prose surfaces (docs/harness/gates-catalog.md, the top-level tools/*.mjs gate scripts, tools/auth-posture.json). tools/check-docs-sync.mjs closes sentence <-> entry BOTH ways and reds an entry whose target this install has reached: at the named release the author must ship the deferred check or move the date in a reviewed diff. This file is harness-owned and git-clean-enforced by check-gate-integrity's tools/ surface, so moving a date is a deliberate act that appears in the PR diff — a date can never roll silently again, which is what happened before this ledger existed: three prose sites carried the same stale promise into the release it named, with nothing reading any of them. `file` is one path or an ARRAY of paths when a single decision is stated at several sites; every listed file must carry the dated sentence, at this entry's exact target. enforcement-tiers.md is deliberately NOT ledgered here — its Target column has its own reader in check-docs-sync.mjs (the surface derivation and the closes: probe) — and SEEDED files are the consumer's prose, not the harness's to red (tools/data-flow.json's export target has its own enforcement in check-data-flow.mjs).

deferrals.reason: The standing ask-the-CLI section census (reading the Supabase CLI's own deprecation warnings instead of a hand-maintained knownSections list). The 0.6.0 spike built it, it worked, and it found the shipped [inbucket] rename — but the blocker is UPSTREAM, not scheduling. RE-CHECKED AT 0.10.0 (2026-08-13), and this is the FIRST firing against a real pin bump rather than an unchanged upstream: npm latest moved 2.113.0 -> 2.114.0 (GA 2026-08-12), so the standing 're-check at every CLI pin bump' clause fired on its own terms. The CLI has been restructured into a pnpm/nx monorepo (apps/cli, apps/cli-go, packages/*) and the Go CLI now lives at apps/cli-go — the path moved, the answer did not: apps/cli-go/cmd/config.go at tag v2.114.0 still registers EXACTLY ONE subcommand, `push` ('Pushes local config.toml to the linked project'), read at the tag rather than inferred from release notes. v2.114.0's config-adjacent changes are a --project-ref flag (#6156), a skip-vault-sync option (#6131) and managed stack persistence (#6152); the TypeScript port now serves `db diff`, `db reset`, `functions download` and `migration squash`, none of which parse config.toml. The exact ask is still open upstream as https://github.com/supabase/cli/issues/5894 ('Add a `supabase config validate` preflight command') — no milestone, no linked PR, zero comments. The original spike findings stand: `functions list` needs an access token, and `status` — the one that runs — binds to whatever stack holds the default ports (it reported another project's containers) and prints SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET into output a gate would then handle. A safe standing check needs a side-effect-free `config lint`-shaped subcommand; re-check for one at every CLI pin bump. THE STANDING RULE (the 0.8.0 move licensed itself 'once'; the 0.9.0 arrival proved the shape recurs, so the rule is now written): each time the target arrives with the upstream condition still unmet, the arrival forces the re-check and the date moves ONE minor in a reviewed diff across every listed site — the scanner's red firing on schedule IS the mechanism, and a discharge happens only when the upstream subcommand actually ships. ARRIVED AT 0.11.0 AND RE-CHECKED, which is what this row's standing rule requires rather than permits: re-checked at 0.11.0 (2026-08-15) against upstream itself rather than against a pin: supabase/cli#5894 'Add a `supabase config validate` preflight command' is still OPEN, still carries no milestone and still has no linked PR implementing it, so the upstream condition — a side-effect-free config-lint-shaped subcommand — remains unmet and the standing rule moves the date ONE minor. Nothing about the spike's original findings has changed — `functions list` still needs an access token and `status` still binds to whatever stack holds the default ports and prints SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET into output a gate would then handle.
